rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The criminals” are those who sever what God commanded to be joined.
rows.anchor: أي القاطعون لما أمر الله به أن يوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They bow their heads in shame, fear, humiliation, and abasement at the place of reckoning.
rows.anchor: أي مطأطئوها خجلا وخوفا وخزيا وذلا في محل المناقشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their Lord is the benefactor who uniquely governs them.
rows.anchor: المحسن إليهم المتوحد بتدبيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They now see what they denied and hear God, the angels, and the fires, becoming certain of divine power and promises.
rows.anchor: ومن أصوات النيران وغير ذلك ما كنا نستبعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to be returned to the abode of earthly deeds so they can act righteously.
rows.anchor: إلى دار الأعمال { نعمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their emphatic certainty answers their earlier doubt; witnessing the scene would reveal horror beyond description or human comprehension.
rows.anchor: مؤكدين لأن حالهم كان حال الشاك الذي يتوقف المخاطب في إيقانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not returned: divine beneficence had emboldened their disobedience, and valid faith must precede direct sight.
rows.anchor: ولأن الإيمان لا يصح إلا بالغيب قبل العيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have granted every accountable soul guidance, right direction, and success in faith and its righteous works, had He willed.
rows.anchor: لأتينا كل نفس } أي مكلفة لأن الكلام فيها { هداها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not will universal guidance because His decree is established; He never fails a promise through incapacity, forgetfulness, or need.
rows.anchor: لأن الإخلاف إما لعجز أو نسيان أو حاجة ولا شيء من ذلك يليق بجنابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears that Hell will be filled with jinn and humans; jinn are named first because people magnified them and they led people astray.
rows.anchor: لأملان جهنم } التي هي محل إهانتي وتجهم اعدائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn are mentioned first to humble them before those who overestimate them, and because they were the ones who misled people.
rows.anchor: أي الجن طائفة إبليس , وكأنه أنثهم تحقيرا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills the disbelievers’ unbelief and sinners’ disobedience after giving them choice and concealing their outcome; acquisition appears theirs, while creation and will belong to Him.
rows.anchor: فصار الكسب ينسب إليهم ظاهرا , والخلق في الحقيقة والمشيئة لي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes the reward as beyond anything an eye has seen, an ear has heard, or a human heart has imagined.
rows.anchor: ما أشار إليه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors have left the circle of faith, the domain of humility and companionship.
rows.anchor: خرجوا عن دائرة الإيمان الذي هو معدن التواضع وأهل للمصاحبة والملازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is their abode, though it is in no respect fit to provide shelter.
rows.anchor: التي لا صلاحية فيها للإيواء بوجه من الوجوه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated efforts to escape add torment by making them imagine escape is possible, like their former flight from evidence and obedience.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه يزاد في عذابهم بأن يخيل إليهم ما يظنون به القدرة على الخروج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When escape seems near, they are effortlessly returned to their former place and this cycle continues forever.
rows.anchor: ولا يزال هذا دأبهم أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to taste the punishment humiliates them; repeated experience makes their former denial still less tenable.
rows.anchor: فإن الإعادة بعد معالجة الخروج أمكن في التصديق باعتبار التجدد في كل آن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises all of them some punishment before the Resurrection, directly and through other agents, including punishment of the grave.
rows.anchor: أي قبل يوم القيامة , بأيديكم وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise answers believers’ human haste for worldly humiliation of their opponents and counters their denial of postmortem punishment and confidence in their numbers and strength.
rows.anchor: بشرهم بذلك على وجه يشمل عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the sūra’s Meccan revelation, God brought Quraysh repeated drought, divided them, and caused them to be killed or captured by believers, among other punishments.
rows.anchor: فأذاقهم الجدب سنين متوالية , وفرق شملهم وقتلهم وأسرهم بأيدي المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter already described.
rows.anchor: أي الذي مر ذكره في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly punishment is meant to make their return from transgression conceivable; many first returned from fear of the sword, then loved Islam after seeing its virtues.
rows.anchor: فلما رأوا محاسن الإسلام كانوا من أشد الناس فيه رغبة وله حبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding argument prepares the claim that there is one governor, as the body has one heart, and that religion comes from God rather than human whim.
rows.anchor: أن مدبر الملك واحد كما أن البدن قلب واحد

rows.speaker: أهل الجاهلية
rows.claim: People of the Jāhiliyya treated ẓihār as an irrevocable permanent divorce; al-Biqāʿī cites Ibn al-Mulaqqin transmitting this from the author of al-Ḥāwī.
rows.anchor: كما نقله ابن الملقن في عمدة المنهاج عن صاحب الحاوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a wife “like my mother’s back” does not make her a mother or permanently forbid her; treating her as one would multiply mothers and make matters unworkable.
rows.anchor: أنت علي كظهر أمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adoption does not confer the inheritance, marriage, or other legal effects of biological sonship; otherwise lineage would be lost and facts confused.
rows.anchor: ليحل لهم إرثكم , وتحرم عليكم حلائلهم وغير ذلك من أحكام الأبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ḥāritha was not the Prophet’s biological son; the Prophet had adopted him after Zayd chose him over his father and family, preparing for the account of his marriage to Zaynab after Zayd divorced her.
rows.anchor: فليس زيد بن حارثة بن شراحيل الكلبي

rows.speaker: المنافقون
rows.claim: The hypocrites objected that Muhammad married the former wife of his son while forbidding this to others; al-Baghawī and others transmit their claim, and the passage answers that adoption is figurative, unlike real sonship and its nursing equivalent.
rows.anchor: قال المنافقون كما حكاه البغوي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had adopted Zayd, who was called Zayd ibn Muḥammad until the command to call adopted children by their fathers was revealed.
rows.anchor: ما كنا ندعوه إلا زيد بن محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adoptive sonship is only a spoken claim, without truth behind it or agreement with the heart; human speech is vulnerable to need, deficiencies, and illusion.
rows.anchor: أي لا حقيقة له وراء القول وتحريك الفم من غير مطابقة قلوبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is surrounded by knowledge and power and possesses all attributes of perfection; unlike human speech, His word is fully true and stable.
rows.anchor: أي المحيط علمه وقدرته وله جميع صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s statements are perfectly true and stable: what He reports matches reality, and no one can defeat His judgment or expose a valid distinction in His analogy.
rows.anchor: فإن أخبر عن شيء فهو كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s utterance precedes and produces its reality by His command; His statements therefore never differ from reality, and He has no bodily organ or need.
rows.anchor: قال قولا وجد مضمونه مطابقا لذلك القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī calls the construction iḥtibāk: “mouth” signals the lack of truth in the first clause, while God’s “truth” signals the negated falsehood in the second; it alludes to human deficiency and divine perfection.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتبك : ذكر الفم أولا دليلا على نفيه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone guides to the complete path that leads to the intended end, so one should not rely on anyone else.
rows.anchor: أي الكامل الذي من شأنه أن يوصل إلى المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their fathers are known, adopted children must be attributed to them; this is closer to justice than adoption, even when adoption arose from compassion, and this rule is central to the sūra’s coming events.
rows.anchor: أي أقرب إلى العدل من التبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their fathers are unknown from original or later ignorance, they are fellow believers if they joined the faith, and clients whether enslaved or freed; Sālim is an example.
rows.anchor: إن كانوا دخلوا في دينكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warned that whoever knowingly claims a father other than his own is barred from Paradise; al-Biqāʿī says al-Bukhārī and Muslim relate it from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and Abū Bakra.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من ادعى إلى غير أبيه وهو يعلم فالجنة عليه حرام )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-blame clause reassures those anxious about earlier mistakes; “error” includes mistakes before or after the prohibition, including mistaken lineage and ẓihār.
rows.anchor: لما كانت عادتهم الخوف مما سبق من أحوالهم على النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “in” indicates error is wholly without sin; “by” might have suggested some sin remained but was merely forgiven.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالظرف ليعيد أن الخطأ لا إثم فيه بوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only intentional action incurs guilt; this wording also removes blame for forgetfulness or a slip of the tongue after the prohibition.
rows.anchor: على سبيل النسيان أو سبق اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the feminine verb as implying that only a heart marked by “feminine softness” would deliberately do this after clarification.
rows.anchor: إلا قلب فيه رخاوة الأنوثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the plural of abundance as extending guilt broadly where deliberate conduct is not prohibited.
rows.anchor: ودل جمع الكثرة على عموم الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness covers the repentant sinner, while His mercy guides the returning errant and grants generosity.
rows.anchor: من صفته الستر البليغ على المذنب النائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge and action encompass all, and He possesses the greatest attributes of majesty, greatness, and might.
rows.anchor: أي وعملكم محيط بأن له مجامع الكبر والعظمة والعز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are beings of purity, nearness, and immunity from sin.
rows.anchor: أي وهم أهل النزهة والقرب والعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike 33:43, which gives God and the angels separate predicates, this verse joins them in one predicate for the Prophet, the highest addressee and head of believers, magnifying the statement.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A joint statement that two people support someone sounds grander than saying separately that one supports him and the other does so too.
rows.anchor: أضخم من قولك : فلان ينصره وفلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ prayer displays the Prophet’s honor and connection to the supreme King through revelation of the wonders of the unseen and visible worlds.
rows.anchor: أي يظهرون شرفه وما له من الوصلة بالملك الأعظم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the angels’ prayer for the Prophet as their invoking blessings; al-Bukhārī transmits this gloss.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كما وراه البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s close implies that believers are also to greet the Prophet, completing the connection conveyed by prayer.
rows.anchor: علم بآخر الكلام أن المعنى : ويسلمون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should promptly and continually display his honor to substantiate their professed faith, as lovers imitate a revered leader.
rows.anchor: بعدم الغفلة عن المبادرة إلى إظهار شرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A great person’s action prompts each lover who recognizes his greatness to imitate him.
rows.anchor: ولأن الكبير إذا فعل شيئا بادر كل محب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greeting the Prophet in the tashahhud is obligatory by consensus and signals submission to all his commands, which is necessary to faith; prayer is sought from God, while greeting comes from the worshipper.
rows.anchor: على الإذعان لجميع أوامره الذي لا يحصل الإيمان إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic command calls for honoring the Prophet as fully as one can through following him, praising him, obeying him, and praying and greeting him as taught.
rows.anchor: أي فأظهورا شرفه بكل ما تصل قدرتكم إليه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وكعب بن عجزة
rows.claim: Traditions from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, and others explain how prayer and greeting unite in displaying the Prophet’s honor.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري وكعب بن عجزة وغيرهما رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives prayer the senses of supplication, mercy, seeking forgiveness, and good praise from God; worshippers’ prayer includes bowing and prostration.
rows.anchor: الصلاة - كما قال في القاموس

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī traces greeting from a wish for life to a judgment or prayer for life, then to any invocation, with conventional use as a greeting.
rows.anchor: كما قال البيضاوي في تفسير سورة النساء

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines greeting as peace, survival, or kingship, and “may God greet you” as “may He preserve you” or “make you king.”
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس : التحية : السلام والبقاء والملك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz says salām is a name of God and here means safety: “peace be upon you” can mean no harm from me, or God’s safety, mercy, or protection from affliction.
rows.anchor: أبو عبد الله القزاز في جامعه : السلام اسم من أسماء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The senses of prayer and greeting converge on displaying honor; al-Bayḍāwī similarly glosses prayer as displaying the Prophet’s honor and greeting as saying peace or submitting to his commands.
rows.anchor: فقد ظهر أن معنى الكل كما ترى ينظر إلى إظهار الشرف

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī interprets prayer as attending to the Prophet’s honor and greeting as either saying peace or submitting to his commands.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فسر البيضاوي يصلون بقوله : يعنتون بإظهار شرفه وتعظيم شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because prayer and greeting share the aim of displaying honor, Biqāʿī applies the word in both literal and figurative senses, following al-Shāfiʿī.
rows.anchor: استعمالا للشيء في حقيقته ومجازه كما هو مذهب إمامنا الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī proposes iḥtibāk: emphasis after “pray” is omitted because the verbal noun after “greet” supplies it; the object of “greet” is omitted because “him” after “pray” supplies it, allowing “greet him” or “submit to him.”
rows.anchor: فتقول : حذف التأكيد أولا لفعل الصلاة لما دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the root and forms of ṣalāt revolve around connection, which underlies the cited interpretations.
rows.anchor: بجميع تراكيبها تدور على الوصلة وهي لازمة لكل ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The citation from 4:43 is one of the examples linked to the preceding claim about using a word in literal and figurative senses.
rows.anchor: ا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited wording about touching women, with references to 4:43 and 5:6, is another example attached to the preceding discussion of literal and figurative usage.
rows.anchor: النساء : 43 , المائدة : 6

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all sustenance depends on the two realms and the question is a reminder and rebuke, God names the heavens in the plural but earth in the singular, since they know no other earth.
rows.anchor: كل شيء من الرزق متوقفا على الكونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They already acknowledge God alone provides sustenance, but this confession has not led them to exclusive worship; the commanded answer confronts them as if they denied it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من المعلوم أنهم مقرون بأن ذلك لله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “God” after the question is the plain conclusion of the proof and exposes the inconsistency between their admission and their worship.
rows.anchor: قل الله } أي الملك الأعلى وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjunctive “or” is not “and”: one party must be on one of two still-unspecified states, guidance or error, a fair challenge that urges careful, unbiased judgment because the stakes are grave.
rows.anchor: أي إن أحد فريقينا على إحدى الحالتين مبهمة غير معنية

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī compares this indirect challenge to telling someone known to be lying that one of us is a liar, or telling a false report’s listener to say “if God wills.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن الجوزي : وهذا كما تقول للرجال تكذبه : والله إن أحدنا لكاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided are compared to riders who can direct their mount where they wish.
rows.anchor: ثم مثل المهتدين بمن هو على متن جواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is like riding above a mount: one follows what is right and can see and avoid anything that might lead to error.
rows.anchor: في متابعة ما ينبغي أن يعمل مستعلين عليه ناظرين لكل ما يمكن أن يعرض فيه مما قد يجر إلى ضلال فتنكبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Error is immersion in mistaken belief about the truth, surrounding its subject so completely that he cannot reach a correct view.
rows.anchor: عن الحق في الاعتقاد المناسب فيه منغمسين فيه وهو محيط بالمبتلى به لا يتمكن معه من وجه صواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manifest error is clear and calls others to recognize it, but the person immersed in it cannot perceive his condition until he steps outside it and sees his conduct lacked reason.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يحس بنفسه وما بينه وبين أن يستبصر

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inclusive challenge urges examination of evidence they had refused, such as their saying that their hearts were covered; it is unusually fair because the speaker includes himself among those who might be right or wrong.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا حث على النظر الذي كانوا يأبونه

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: خالد بن الوليد وعمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Khalid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said they had once been astonished when anyone entered Islam, but now were astonished when anyone hesitated about it.
rows.anchor: كخالد بن الوليد وعمرو بن العاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents openly claim that they are guided and the Muslims astray, the response is even fairer: neither side demands an account from the other, and each may follow the way that becomes clear.
rows.anchor: أمره أن يجيبهم على هذا التقدير بما هو أبلغ في الإنصاف من الأول

words: لَّا تُسْـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجْرَمْنَا وَلَا نُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers say they will not be questioned by their opponents about their own errors, nor question the opponents’ deeds; they leave them and others to follow whichever path is clear.
rows.anchor: فاتركونا والناس غيركم كما أنا نحن تاركوكم

words: قل يجمع بيننا ربنا ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will bring the parties together under His judgment, arranged by His decree, in this world or the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: في قضائه المرتب على قدره في الدنيا أو في الآخرة
